title: North

pages.message: Every summer the Arctic ice cap melts down to what scientists call its "minimum" before colder weather begins to cause ice cover to increase.
As the planet warms and polar ice melts, our global average sea level is rising.

note: Ours: the September average of every year, the month of the Arctic minimum, against its 1981–2010 normal, with the global mean sea level (12-month mean centered on September 1, change since 1993). Sea ice is shown as a sign of polar ice melt; its amount does not drive the sea level values.

title: South

pages.message: This visualization shows the daily Antarctic sea ice and seasonal land cover change progressing through time
As the planet warms and polar ice melts, our global average sea level is rising.

note: Ours: the February average of every year, the month of the Antarctic minimum, against its 1981–2010 normal, with the global mean sea level (12-month mean centered on September 1, change since 1993). Sea ice is shown as a sign of polar ice melt; its amount does not drive the sea level values.
